description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

The transcript describes a dangerous incident in 1982 involving a shotgun and large saguaro cacti in Arizona. A man and a friend went to the desert for target practice, shot several cacti, and then hit a large 26-foot specimen—an arm snapped off and fell directly on him, likely causing fatal impact or severe injury; the remoteness made help difficult. The transcript also mentions another saguaro-related shooting incident in 2012 where the person survived but needed extensive medical treatment. What other “survival lessons” from weird incidents should we cover next?
